scope_reason: The paper examines the flood and drought (inundation) regime of a wetland and its hydroclimatic drivers, including extreme rainfall.

scope_span.evidence_text: we sought to identify the main hydroclimatic determinants of the strongly episodic flood regime of a large catchment in the semi-arid, subtropical northwest of Australia

claims.restatement: Severe and intense regional rainfall events, plus the sequence of recharge events within and between years, determine surface water expression on the floodplain.

concept.value: surface water expression on the floodplain

relation_or_direction.value: determined by severe and intense regional rainfall events and the sequence of recharge events

geography.value: Fortescue Marsh, upper Fortescue River catchment, Pilbara, northwest Australia

support_span.evidence_text: We used a monthly sequence of satellite images to quantify surface water expression on the Fortescue Marsh, the largest water feature of inland northwest Australia, from 1988 to 2012.

evidence.evidence_text: We found that severe and intense regional rainfall events, as well as the sequence of recharge events both within and between years, determine surface water expression on the floodplain

claims.restatement: The most severe inundation of the last century, about 1000 km2, was recorded in 2000.

geography.value: Fortescue Marsh, upper Fortescue River catchment, Pilbara, northwest Australia

support_span.evidence_text: We used a monthly sequence of satellite images to quantify surface water expression on the Fortescue Marsh, the largest water feature of inland northwest Australia, from 1988 to 2012.

evidence.evidence_text: The most severe inundation (∼ 1000 km 2 ) over the last century was recorded in 2000.

claims.restatement: The Fortescue Marsh was completely dry in 32% of all years, for periods of up to four consecutive years.

relation_or_direction.value: 32% of all years; up to four consecutive years

support_span.evidence_text: We used this sequence together with instrumental rainfall data to build a multiple linear model and reconstruct monthly history of floods and droughts since 1912.

evidence.evidence_text: The Fortescue Marsh was completely dry for 32 % of all years, for periods of up to four consecutive years.

claims.restatement: Inundation duration, severity and frequency during 1999-2006 were above average and unprecedented relative to the last century.

concept.value: duration, severity and frequency of inundations

geography.value: Fortescue Marsh, upper Fortescue River catchment, Pilbara, northwest Australia

support_span.evidence_text: We used a monthly sequence of satellite images to quantify surface water expression on the Fortescue Marsh, the largest water feature of inland northwest Australia, from 1988 to 2012.

evidence.evidence_text: Duration, severity and frequency of inundations between 1999 and 2006 were above average and unprecedented when compared to the last century.

claims.restatement: Recent flooding-regime changes suggest the wetland will become more persistent as extreme rainfall events increase in frequency and intensity, likely impacting the ecosystem's structure and functioning.

concept.value: wetland persistence; ecosystem structure and functioning

relation_or_direction.value: suggest will become more persistent in response to increased frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall; will likely impact

support_span.evidence_text: the Fortescue Marsh, the largest water feature of inland northwest Australia

temporal_frame.value: over the last 20 years (basis); future unspecified

evidence.evidence_text: changes to the flooding regime over the last 20 years suggest that the wetland will become more persistent in response to increased frequency and intensity of extreme rainfall events for the region, which in turn will likely impact on the structure and functioning of this highly specialized ecosystem.

rejected_or_ambiguous.evidence_text: Extreme climatic events such as tropical cyclones, heavy rainfall and severe drought are projected to become more intense and less frequent globally over the next hundred years in response to anthropogenic-driven climate change (Coumou and Rahmstorf, 2012).
rejected_or_ambiguous.reason: Cited background projection, not examined by the paper.

rejected_or_ambiguous.evidence_text: A simple linear regression between time and yearly duration of floods (F A > 0 km 2 ) further demonstrates slightly increased inundation length since the beginning of the century (p value = 0.046).
rejected_or_ambiguous.reason: Authors themselves say it should be treated with caution (non-independence, n = 25).

rejected_or_ambiguous.evidence_text: Droughts of at least one year were frequent (21 %) between 1912-2012
rejected_or_ambiguous.reason: Not promoted; its relation to the abstract's 32% dry-year figure (claim C3) is not explained in the text.
